INTERACTION HOTSPOTS — where each species lives and what it does (research: AQ-45)
Clownfish hosts in bubble-tip anemone (low, left island) — obligate symbiosis; defends its anemone.
Blue-green chromis school above branching Acropora — dive into branches when startled.
Lyretail anthias shoal above the right crest — open-water plankton pickers; Acropora is their bunker.
Royal gramma claims a cave / ledge — belly-to-rock, often upside-down under the ceiling.
Banggai cardinalfish hovers by branching coral — slow, cover-bound; retreats into branches.
Firefish hovers above its sand burrow in the valley — darts in at the first sign of danger.
Yellow watchman goby stands lookout at its burrow mouth — shared burrow with a pistol shrimp.
Mandarin dragonet hops across low rubble — slow copepod hunter, hugging the substrate.
Tailspot blenny perches on a rock ledge — grazes film algae, darts into a hole when startled.
Yellow tang grazes algae along the rock face — daytime grazer, rests in a crevice at night.
Six-line wrasse patrols crevices — stop-and-go hunting loops through the rockwork.
Copperband butterflyfish probes crevices with its long snout — picks at polyps and pests.
Flame angelfish grazes rock and sponge — roams the reef face, nips fleshy coral (with caution).
Blue tang (valley lane) — open-water cruiser; juveniles shelter in branching coral.
